Subject: Request: Custom SLA Exhibit for OrbisAI enterprise agreement

Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement & legal asked me to follow up with a request: OrbisAI needs a formal SLA exhibit attached to the enterprise MSA that captures three items we consider critical for our production rollout:

1) Uptime commitment with narrow maintenance windows: we need clarity on scheduled maintenance notice and whether planned maintenance is considered an exclusion for uptime credits.
2) Latency SLOs by workload class: for our low-latency chat endpoints we need p95 < 250ms under normal load and p95 < 350ms under peak (our peak is 5–8pm ET). For bulk embedding/batch jobs we accept higher tails.
3) Degraded-mode handling & regional failover: if a region is degraded, we want automatic routing to a fallback region, plus a credit schedule if failover impacts throughput/latency beyond agreed thresholds.

Attached are the draft MSA and a proposed order form with placeholders (OrbisAI_Draft_MSA_v3.pdf, OrbisAI_SLA_Exhibit_Draft.docx, OrbisAI_OrderForm_Summary.xlsx). Can your team propose specific exhibit language and an order form snippet we can circulate to our legal team? Also: what evidence will you provide for latency/uptime (monthly dashboard, raw traces, SOC2 logs)?

We aim to finalize this before our board meeting on Feb 1.

Thanks,
Sophie Kendall
Sr. Procurement Manager
OrbisAI

Sophie —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attachments. High level response and a couple quick clarifying questions before we draft language:

- Maintenance and notice: our standard is 48 hours notice for scheduled maintenance that affects production; planned maintenance windows are excluded from uptime calculations only when notice is provided and the work is published to the status page. We can draft a customer-specific exhibit that changes notice to 72 hours if that is required.

- Latency SLOs: we track p50/p95/p99 per-route and can commit a p95 target for the routed chat endpoints. The numbers you requested (p95 < 250ms normal, < 350ms peak) are achievable in our Dedicated offering in the us-east-1 region with a routing SLA. For Hosted customers we typically include a clause that latency targets apply when requests are routed to the Dedicated or equivalent configured pool; if we need this to apply to hosted tiers we will need to size capacity on day one (we can include an order form commitment for reserved throughput).

- Evidence: we can provide a monthly latency/uptime dashboard (CSV export), raw aggregated request histograms for the agreed routes, and availability alerts with incident timelines. We do not share raw customer payloads; logs are anonymized and include request ids, timestamps, route, and latency.

Next steps I propose: I will loop in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (CS/onboarding) and ask for two draft options: (A) minimal exhibit that adjusts notice and credit schedule, and (B) a stronger exhibit that includes order-form reserved throughput and an explicit regional failover credit table. Please let me know which direction Orbis prefers.

Best,

Michael / Laura —

Attached below are two proposed exhibit drafts and an order form snippet. I kept the language modular so we can flip between Option A and Option B in the MSA exhibit. Highlights:

Option A (minimal edits) — Scheduled Maintenance: Redwood will provide no less than 48 hours’ notice for scheduled maintenance that may materially affect production. Scheduled maintenance will not be considered an Availability Incident if (i) notice was published to the status page at least 48 hours prior to the window, and (ii) maintenance occurs within the published window.

Latency SLOs: For routes explicitly identified in the Order Form as "Chat (low-latency)", Redwood commits to monthly p95 latency not to exceed 250ms during Normal Operating Periods. During Peak Windows (defined in the Order Form) the committed p95 shall not exceed 350ms. Breaches are subject to the credit schedule below.

Degraded Mode and Regional Failover: "Degraded Mode" means the inability to serve requests from the Primary Region at the Target Throughput for a continuous period of >5 minutes. In the event Redwood initiates automatic routing to a designated Failover Region, Redwood will: (a) trigger the failover within the documented mitigation timeline, (b) notify OrbisAI via the status page and email within 15 minutes, and (c) provide a post-incident report within 48 hours. Credits apply when regional failover results in sustained p95 degradations beyond the committed thresholds.

Credit Schedule (example):
- Availability < 99.9% in a calendar month = 5% of monthly fee per 0.1% below 99.9% (capped at 50%).
- p95 breaches for Chat Route: first breach = notice and remediation plan; second breach within 30 days = 2% monthly fee credit; third = 5%.

Option B (reserved throughput + tighter commitments) — includes a line in the Order Form committing a baseline reserved TPS and memory footprint for chat routes; latency commitments are guaranteed when reserved capacity is in effect. Option B also adds an explicit maintenance notice of 72 hours if Orbis requests longer notice.

Evidence: Redwood will provide a monthly availability & latency export (CSV), aggregated per-route histograms, and a secure link to anonymized traces for incidents. SOC2 evidence remains available via the standard attestation process; audit logs can be provided under an evidence-sharing addendum.

I attached two doc versions with redlines and an Order Form snippet you can paste into the MSA (OrbisAI_SLA_Exhibit_Draft_v2.docx, OrbisAI_OrderForm_Snippet.docx). Also added a sample clause for automatic failover sequencing.

If we go Option B, Ops will need a 2–4 week lead time to provision reserved capacity depending on sizing.
